title: Trump widens battle with the press, banning CNN and others from White House
text:
Trump widens battle with the press, banning CNN and others from White House
President Donald Trump announced a ban on three major news outlets – CNN, Politico, and MS NOW – calling them purveyors of “fake news.”
President Donald Trump has banned three major news outlets – CNN, Politico, and MS NOW – from the White House, effective immediately.
The move, announced Friday afternoon in a post on Truth Social, was unexpected and raises serious questions about press freedom in the United States.
In the statement, President Trump said he was banning the three outlets from the White House “as a result of their constant ‘reporting’ FAKE NEWS!” and added that more bans are coming.
President Donald Trump’s move to restrict prominent news organizations heightens questions about press freedom that have been growing in his second term.
“Media Outlets shouldn’t be able to constantly write or report FICTION and LIES when they’re covering the President of the United States, the Trump Administration, or the United States of America,” Mr. Trump continued. “Other Fake News Media Outlets to follow.”
The president has been testing the boundaries of the U.S. Constitution’s First Amendment right to freedom of the press almost from the start of his second term. In February 2025, the White House banned The Associated Press from participating in the rotation of reporters covering the president that represents the wider press corps, known as the “pool,” in the Oval Office, on Air Force One, and other venues with limited space.
The AP was banned from the press pool for a period over its decision not to refer to the Gulf of Mexico as the “Gulf of America.” Per a federal court order, the wire service was readmitted into the pool two months later, in April 2025, but the AP’s lawsuit over the ban is ongoing. Mr. Trump has sued other outlets over their coverage, including The New York Times, The Wall Street Journal, and the BBC.
As of 4 p.m. Eastern time, about an hour after Mr. Trump’s announcement, no one had been evicted from the White House briefing room, according to print pool reporter Philip Wang of Time magazine.
Early Friday evening, the White House Correspondents’ Association (WHCA) weighed in.
“The Constitution protects the freedom of the press from government interference,” Jacqui Heinrich of Fox News, the WHCA president, said in a statement. “That protection does not depend on whether the president likes a news organization’s coverage, agrees with its reporting, or approves of the questions its journalists ask.”
At stake, she said, are not just the rights of journalists but also the public’s right to information about those who hold the nation’s highest office.
Friday’s announcement comes after a restrictive move against the Pentagon press corps last October, when Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth instituted a requirement that reporters cover only pre-approved news. More than 30 reporters staged an unprecedented walkout and relinquished their Pentagon press passes.
And last month, a federal judge upheld the Pentagon’s ability to fire three high-level staff members at the military newspaper Stars and Stripes following the staff’s pushback against censorship.
PEN America, an organization dedicated to global freedom of expression, issued a statement Friday after Mr. Trump’s announcement.
“Someone needs to explain to President Trump how the First Amendment works,” said Tim Richardson, journalism and disinformation director at PEN America. “As we’ve seen time and time again, this administration’s hostility toward the press is never about the accuracy of news stories, but about its inability to withstand scrutiny of its actions. The White House can’t be allowed to decide which journalists are able to cover the president based on the content of their news coverage.”
In an exchange with reporters in the Oval Office late Friday, Mr. Trump was asked whether the press ban would survive a court challenge.
“I don’t think that a court should allow fake news to be written day after day after day,” the president said.
At time of writing, the three banned outlets were expected to sue.
Editor’s note: This article was updated on Sept. 18, the date of initial publication, to include a comment from the White House Correspondents’ Association.
